newsitem.title: FRANCE: French journalists to strike for tax break.
newsitem.headline: French journalists to strike for tax break.

text.p: French journalists will vote with their pens, cameras and microphones Tuesday when many stop work for a day to demand the government drop plans to scrap a 62-year-old tax break for their profession.
All the main journalists' unions have called a 24-hour work stoppage in defence of a 30 percent income tax deduction for professional expenses, which they say is effectively part of their salary.

The government plans to phase out the journalists' deduction over five years, along with dozens of other breaks for various professions as part of a reform that will cut income tax for most taxpayers.
The unions say journalists earning the profession's average wage of 12,000 francs ($2,320) a month will lose the equivalent of a month's net pay.
In the most extreme case, a single journalist earning 15,000 francs ($2,900) a month will end up paying 60 percent more tax after the reform, government figures show.
Unions representing nearly 30,000 journalists have called a demonstration outside parliament as the National Assembly begins debating the 1997 budget bill.
The strike call has strong support in the public broadcast media and the regional press, but less backing in the national daily press and at private broadcasters, union officials say.

Several regional dailies are unlikely to appear Wednesday as a result and newscasts on public radio and television stations are likely to be limited to a minimum service. The strike is also expected to restrict French-language news services from the news agencies, Agence France-Presse and Reuters, union sources said.
